{{Short description|Mathematical integration method}}
In mathematics, in the field of [[p-adic analysis]], the '''Volkenborn integral''' is a method of [[integral|integration]] for p-adic functions.

== Definition ==
Let :<math>f:\Z_p\to \Complex_p</math> be a function from the [[P-adic number|p-adic]] integers taking values in the p-adic numbers. The Volkenborn integral is defined by the limit, if it exists:

:<math> \int_{\Z_p} f(x) \, {\rm d}x = \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{p^n} \sum_{x=0}^{p^n-1} f(x). </math>

More generally, if

:<math> R_n = \left\{\left. x = \sum_{i=r}^{n-1} b_i p^i \right | b_i=0, \ldots, p-1 \text{ for } r<n \right\} </math>

then 

:<math> \int_K f(x) \, {\rm d}x = \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{p^n} \sum_{x \in R_n \cap K} f(x). </math>

This integral was defined by Arnt Volkenborn.

== Examples ==
:<math> \int_{\Z_p} 1 \, {\rm d}x = 1 </math>
:<math> \int_{\Z_p} x \, {\rm d}x = -\frac{1}{2} </math>
:<math> \int_{\Z_p} x^2 \, {\rm d}x = \frac{1}{6} </math>
:<math> \int_{\Z_p} x^k \, {\rm d}x = B_k</math>

where <math>B_k</math> is the k-th [[Bernoulli number]].

The above four examples can be easily checked by direct use of the definition and [[Faulhaber's formula]].

:<math> \int_{\Z_p} {x \choose k} \, {\rm d}x = \frac{(-1)^k}{k+1} </math>
:<math> \int_{\Z_p} (1 + a)^x \, {\rm d}x = \frac{\log(1+a)}{a} </math>
:<math> \int_{\Z_p} e^{a x} \, {\rm d}x = \frac{a}{e^a-1} </math>

The last two examples can be formally checked by expanding in the [[Taylor series]] and integrating term-wise.

:<math> \int_{\Z_p} \log_p(x+u) \, {\rm d}u = \psi_p(x)</math>

with <math>\log_p</math> the p-adic logarithmic function and <math>\psi_p </math> the p-adic [[digamma function]].

== Properties ==
:<math> \int_{\Z_p} f(x+m) \, {\rm d}x = \int_{\Z_p} f(x) \, {\rm d}x+ \sum_{x=0}^{m-1} f'(x)</math>

From this it follows that the Volkenborn-integral is not translation invariant.

If <math>P^t = p^t \Z_p</math> then 

:<math> \int_{P^t} f(x) \, {\rm d}x = \frac{1}{p^t} \int_{\Z_p} f(p^t x) \, {\rm d}x</math>

== Origin ==
The idea of integrating p-adic functions was initially proposed by F. Thomas and [[François Bruhat]].
However, the definition of their translation-invariant p-adic integral proved too restrictive for analytical and number-theoretical purposes.
Arnt Volkenborn developed the generalized p-adic integral, later named after him, in his 1971 dissertation at the [[University of Cologne]]. The Volkenborn integral allows integration of all locally analytic functions, such as [[Laurent series]]. It is used in the computation of the generalized p-adic Bernoulli numbers (like in the examples above) and other p-adic functions.
